## SECTION B: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY (Plain Language)

This is the biggest folder in the project (235 files) and one of the simplest to describe: it is how the browser looks and what it is called. It repaints the interface deep black with cyan text and a pink active tab, sets a nebula wallpaper, and renames every visible 'Firefox'/'Mozilla' to 'Gorilla'/'Gorilla Unleashed'. The one real engineering idea is that the theme is built to cost the graphics chip almost nothing — it uses only effects the chip handles by itself and switches animations off, so the styled look does not drain a 2012 laptop's battery. It is safe to ship: nothing here touches your data or the network. The automated pre-check flagged 31 files that only remove a blank line under the copyright header — those were inspected and confirmed to be an intentional tidy-up, not lost text. The mass 'Gorilla' renaming is the project owner's deliberate branding, not a mistake.

## SECTION C: TECHNICAL SUMMARY (Developer)

Cosmetic + identity layer, no behaviour/network/data surface. Theme delivery: master-redirect.css (315 lines, NEW_FILE) injected via a single @import at browser-shared.css:36; palette #000000/#00FFFF (cyan)/#FFC0CB (pink active tab); transitions/animations neutralised to 0.01ms; enforces the project CSS invariants (opacity/transform only, outline not border, no XUL scale transforms, will-change:auto globally, contain:layout style). findbar.css covers the chrome://global/skin widgets master-redirect.css cannot reach; jar.inc.mn packages master-redirect.css + nebula.jpg. Rebrand: 166 of 235 patches carry added 'Gorilla' strings (2535 added branded lines); 0 doubled brand in patch bodies or the live en-US tree; 31 patches are structural-only blank-line-under-MPL-header strips (== the 31 pre-check P1s, confirmed intentional); the remaining ~38 add non-brand mechanical-integrity lines (menubar re-adds 63 .accesskey lines; browser.ftl re-adds 10 {$engine} placeable lines — the 2026-08-04 restorations). Three corrections vs the gen-1 (2026-07-17) audit are folded in: design-system dist is vanilla (0 Gorilla/#00FFFF hits) and is NOT the palette source of truth; warning.svg is stock/unapplied (1.5 MB patch dropped 2026-08-04); the 'palette also in tokens' P3 is therefore moot — master-redirect.css is the sole palette source.

## SECTION F: PHASED PLAN

### Phase 1 — `browser/locales + toolkit/locales`
- **Change:** Script the rebrand as a deterministic find-replace with the FTL-safety guards baked in, so a version bump re-applies it reproducibly across the 235-file surface instead of by hand.
- **Expected impact:** Makes the largest, most regression-prone surface reproducible.

### Phase 0 — `master-redirect.css`
- **Change:** Add the top-of-file boundary comment and keep the palette as the single source of truth (tokens are vanilla by design).
- **Expected impact:** Removes the non-obvious maintenance trap without re-introducing a second palette source.

### Phase 2 — `patches/lint`
- **Change:** Add the FTL-structural preflight to CI so the four known-fatal patterns fail the build.
- **Expected impact:** Turns a class of historically-fatal, silent regressions into a hard build error.

## POSITIVE OBSERVATIONS

- The zero-CPU constraint is a genuine engineering idea, not decoration: visual richness (colour/contrast/wallpaper) is free to render; motion is what costs CPU, and motion is exactly what the theme forgoes.
- The palette has one source of truth (master-redirect.css) and the design-system tokens were correctly left vanilla — verified 0 Gorilla/#00FFFF hits in dist.
- The chrome-skin vs global-skin boundary is correctly handled: findbar.css exists precisely because master-redirect.css physically cannot reach those widgets.
- The rebrand is correctly scoped and clean: it is the legitimate public product name in user-visible strings (the intended exception to the no-new-gorilla-identifiers code rule), with zero doubled brand and zero lost messages.
- The build made the honest call on warning.svg: a 1.5 MB warning icon contradicts the low-memory target, so the tree keeps the 1223 B stock icon and the overreaching patch was dropped.

# ═══ MERGED DOCUMENT: 08-look.DEVELOPER.md (gen-2 · verbatim · sha256:be58e6f446642990 · merged 2026-08-04) ═══

# 08.Look — Zero-CPU chrome theme (master-redirect.css) + 166-file en-US Gorilla rebrand + branding-asset delivery

> Generated 2026-08-04 | Source: `08.Look`

---

## Purpose

The visual-identity layer of the build: it repaints the browser chrome into the Gorilla palette and renames every user-visible 'Firefox'/'Mozilla' string to 'Gorilla'/'Gorilla Unleashed'. Trust level: cosmetic. No behaviour, no network, no data path is introduced by any file here. 235 patch files: 121 under browser/locales/en-US, 111 under toolkit/locales/en-US, and 3 theme files (browser-shared.css, jar.inc.mn, findbar.css). Branding binary assets (nebula.jpg, icons, fonts) ship as NEW_FILES under browser/branding/gorilla and are wired in by the mozconfig branding flag owned by Topic 05.

## Design Rationale

The governing constraint is zero CPU-side layout recalculation: the chrome must render on the Intel HD 4000 GPU without waking the CPU for a reflow. Visual richness (colour, contrast, wallpaper) is GPU-native and free; motion and box-model change are CPU-bound and are therefore forbidden. This is why the theme is a bold static palette with animations neutralised to 0.01ms rather than an animated theme. The rebrand is delivered as a mechanical per-file en-US diff rather than a runtime string map so it is auditable one file at a time and travels with the patch set.

## Architecture

- **Pattern:** Injected override stylesheet (master-redirect.css loaded via a single @import into browser chrome) + a boundary stylesheet (findbar.css) for widgets on the chrome://global/skin path + a mechanical locale rebrand across en-US .ftl/.properties files.
- **Trust boundary:** None crossed — cosmetic layer. One clarification: the Firefox->Gorilla rename is legitimate public product identity and is the intended exception to the project-wide no-new-gorilla-identifiers rule, which governs NEW code identifiers and filenames, not user-visible product-name strings.
- **Attack surface:** N/A — no entry point, no parser of untrusted input, no privileged operation is added here. The only integrity concern is self-inflicted: FTL structural breakage during the rebrand (see error_conditions).
- **Dependencies:** `mozconfig branding flag (Topic 05) -> browser/branding/gorilla`, `Topic 07 LightweightThemeManager lock (theme cannot be user-swapped)`, `browser/themes/shared/browser-shared.css (host of the @import)`, `browser/themes/shared/jar.inc.mn (packages master-redirect.css + nebula.jpg into chrome://browser/skin/)`

## Flags & Configuration

| Name | Type | Default | Effect | Notes |
|------|------|---------|--------|-------|
| `@import master-redirect.css` | `string` | `present at browser-shared.css:36 (live) / added at browser-shared.css.patch:15` | Loads the entire chrome theme. Removing the line disables the paint job wholesale. | Must sit in a LEADING @import block; an @import placed after style rules is silently dropped (GOLDEN_RULES C9/C10; THEME_FIX_LOG section 1). |
| `color-scheme: dark` | `string` | `dark (forced)` | Forces chrome to the dark branch so light-dark() tokens resolve to readable values over the black background. | master-redirect.css; without it FF154 light-dark() tokens paint near-black text on black. |

## API Surface

| Symbol | Description | Side Effects |
|--------|-------------|--------------|
| `master-redirect.css` | Palette remap + animation neutralisation + FF154 renamed-token overrides + native context-menu/popup restoration. | Repaints all chrome; sets transition/animation durations to 0.01ms. |
| `browser-shared.css.patch` | Delivery point for the theme. | Adds NO hard-coded palette hexes (0 lines add #00FFFF/#000000); palette resolves through var() indirection to master-redirect.css. |
| `menubar.ftl.patch / browser.ftl.patch` | Representative of the mechanical-integrity restorations: menubar.ftl.patch re-adds 63 .accesskey lines; browser.ftl.patch re-adds 10 {$engine}-bearing placeable lines. | Restores menu accesskeys and the search-engine placeable that earlier mechanical breakage had eaten; branding co-present (176 Gorilla lines in browser.ftl.patch). |

## Kill Switches

### `browser-shared.css:36 (@import master-redirect.css)`
- **Condition:** always, at chrome load
- **Effect:** Injects the palette remap + animation neutralisation into browser chrome.
- reversible
- Single line of delivery; loaded via chrome://browser/skin/ and therefore cannot reach chrome://global/skin/ widgets.

### `toolkit/themes/shared/findbar.css (patch)`
- **Condition:** always
- **Effect:** Styles the find bar and related global-skin widgets master-redirect.css cannot reach.
- reversible
- Exists precisely because of the chrome-skin vs global-skin path boundary. This is now the SOLE global-skin styling patch: the former warning.svg patch was dropped (see dead_code).

### `browser/themes/shared/jar.inc.mn (patch)`
- **Condition:** build/packaging
- **Effect:** Packages master-redirect.css and nebula.jpg into chrome://browser/skin/.
- reversible
- Two added lines; without them the stylesheet and wallpaper are not shipped even if present in-tree.

## Dead Code

- **`toolkit/themes/shared/icons/warning.svg patch (REMOVED)`** — The 1.54 MB single-line custom SVG was never applied to the live tree; live warning.svg is byte-identical to vanilla (1223 B). The gen-1 docs overclaimed 'findbar.css + warning.svg'. The patch was dropped on 2026-08-04. (risk: None from removal — a 1.5 MB warning icon contradicts the low-memory target; the tree state (stock) is the correct one.)

## Performance

- **CPU:** The governing metric. Chrome renders on the GPU; no animation/transition wakes the CPU for a reflow. Not benchmarked as a number here.
- **MEMORY:** master-redirect.css uses will-change: auto globally to stop WebRender over-promoting layers into the HD 4000's UMA-shared VRAM; contain: layout style isolates reflows without breaking XUL flexbox. nebula.jpg is 117702 bytes, loaded once at startup.
- **IO:** Branding assets (nebula.jpg, fonts, logos) loaded once at startup; no recurring I/O.
- **NOTES:** Reference machine is 16 GiB DDR3L UMA-shared with the HD 4000; distribution audience is ~4 GB. The VRAM-economy rules matter more on the distribution target than on the reference machine.

## Security

- **Remote execution:** None. No code path added.
- **Data handling:** None. No data read, stored, or transmitted.
- **Attack surface:** N/A — cosmetic + static text.
- **Notes:** The only failure mode is self-inflicted FTL breakage; the Fluent parser gate is the control for it.

## Error Conditions

| Error | Cause | Remedy |
|-------|-------|--------|
| `Blank/invisible window at runtime` | FTL structural damage: text edited inside < > tags breaks data-l10n-name -> DOM hydration; or a blank line between a Fluent value and its .description attribute. | Never edit text inside tags; keep value/.description adjacency; rebuild and confirm Fluent parser reports 0 junk. |
| `.title swallowed into a multiline .label` | A .title attribute indented under a multiline .label value (the reportBrokenSite historical hazard). | Keep .label single-line + separate .title; the live tree already carries the corrected form. |
| `Doubled brand ('Gorilla Gorilla')` | An automated rebrand pass applied twice. | grep -lE '^[+].*Gorilla Gorilla' *.patch must be 0; verified 0 in both the patch bodies and the live en-US locales. |

## Tasks

### Verify the rebrand surface is clean and correctly scoped

Run before shipping a version bump; the 235-file surface is the most regression-prone in the project.

**Prerequisites:**
- Working copy of patches/new.patches/08.Look
- FF_SRC pointed at the built tree

**Step 1:** grep -lE '^[+].*Gorilla' *.patch | wc -l
  - Expected: 166 (branding-bearing patches).
**Step 2:** grep -lE '^[+].*(Gorilla Gorilla|Unleashed Unleashed)' *.patch | wc -l
  - Expected: 0 (no doubled brand).
**Step 3:** Count zero-add patches (structural-only strips): for f in *.patch; do [ "$(grep -cE '^[+][^+]' "$f")" = 0 ] && echo "$f"; done | wc -l
  - Expected: 31 — the blank-line-under-MPL-header strips; these are the 31 precheck P1s.

**After this task:** Branding volume matches (166); no doubled brand; the 31 pure-deletions are accounted for as intentional.

### Verify the theme-delivery chain end to end

Confirm the paint job is actually injected and packaged, not merely present in-tree.

**Prerequisites:**
- Built tree at $FF_SRC

**Step 1:** grep -n master-redirect $FF_SRC/browser/themes/shared/browser-shared.css
  - Expected: line 36: @import url("chrome://browser/skin/master-redirect.css"); in the leading import block.
**Step 2:** grep -cE 'color-scheme|#00FFFF|0\.01ms' $FF_SRC/browser/themes/shared/master-redirect.css
  - Expected: ~30 marker hits (palette + animation neutralisation present).
**Step 3:** grep -nE 'master-redirect|nebula' patches/new.patches/08.Look/browser_themes_shared_jar.inc.mn.patch
  - Expected: both packaged into skin/classic/browser/.

**After this task:** @import present in a leading block; palette markers present; assets packaged.

### Confirm the design-system tokens are vanilla (not a second palette source)

Corrects the gen-1 claim that semantic-categories.mjs/tokens-table.mjs are the palette source of truth.

**Prerequisites:**
- Built tree at $FF_SRC

**Step 1:** grep -rEl 'Gorilla|#00FFFF|#FFC0CB' $FF_SRC/toolkit/themes/shared/design-system/dist/ | wc -l
  - Expected: 0 — dist restored to vanilla; no Gorilla palette content.

**After this task:** The palette has exactly one source of truth: master-redirect.css.

## Troubleshooting

**Symptom:** Urlbar text black-on-black / toolbars pale
**Cause:** FF154 renamed the toolbar/field CSS variables; master-redirect forced only the legacy names.
**Remedy:** Force the current names (--toolbar-background-color, --toolbar-field-text-color, etc.) in the :root block.
**Verify:** THEME_FIX_LOG section 3; grep the packaged master-redirect.css for the renamed tokens.

**Symptom:** Find bar or arrow-panel pop-ups unstyled/black-on-black
**Cause:** Widget loads via chrome://global/skin/ (unreachable by master-redirect) or re-declares --panel-text-color at element level.
**Remedy:** findbar.css covers the find bar; element-level !important panel blocks cover the pop-ups (THEME_FIX_LOG section 14).
**Verify:** grep -c popupnotification on the packaged master-redirect.css.

**Symptom:** Hidden hero/promo art paints over an about: page
**Cause:** Missing FF154 :where([hidden]){display:none!important} rule in the shared in-content CSS.
**Remedy:** Restore the [hidden] rule (global-shared.css:34 carries it live as of 2026-08-04).
**Verify:** grep -n ':where(\[hidden\])' $FF_SRC/toolkit/themes/shared/global-shared.css.

## Technical Debt

🟠 **MEDIUM** — 235-file locale surface is regression-prone on version bumps → Add an FTL-structural preflight that fails on (a) edited text inside < >, (b) blank line before a .description, (c) 'Gorilla Gorilla' doubles, (d) .title indented under multiline .label. Cheap; catches every historically-fatal pattern.
🟡 **LOW** — chrome-skin vs global-skin split (master-redirect.css vs findbar.css) is a non-obvious boundary → Add a top-of-file comment in master-redirect.css noting it cannot reach chrome://global/skin/ and pointing to findbar.css.
🟡 **LOW** — reportBrokenSite.ftl.patch is a stale record → Regenerate that one patch from the live tree (live is authoritative and carries the corrected .label/.title form); do not rebuild the tree from the stale patch.

## Impact If Removed

Reverting the folder: the browser looks and is named like stock Firefox; default animations return and wake the CPU on the HD 4000 during ordinary interaction; the find bar and global-skin pop-ups lose their matching style; the nebula wallpaper, custom logos and Gorilla name disappear. No functional capability is lost — the layer is cosmetic and identity-only.

# The Look — a distinctive black-and-cyan identity, and a full rename to Gorilla Unleashed, built to cost the graphics chip almost nothing — Plain Language Guide

> Generated 2026-08-04 from `08.Look`

---

## Should You Run This?

Yes. This is cosmetic-and-rename work with no data, network, or security surface. The one historical risk — breaking a text file so a window blanks — is checked by an automated parser that currently reports clean. If you dislike the specific colours or the name, they are the easiest things in the whole project to change.

## Worst Case, Honestly

The realistic worst case is cosmetic, not a security or privacy risk. If a text file's structure were broken by a careless edit, a window could render blank or a menu item could go missing — inconvenient, and it has happened before in this project's history, which is exactly why the text edits are checked so carefully. As currently built, the automated Fluent parser reports zero broken entries, zero duplicate names, and zero lost messages.

## What Data This Touches

Nothing here touches your data, sends anything, or stores anything about you. It is paint and names. Every colour and every renamed word is rendered locally on your own machine. There is no network use and no tracking introduced by any file in this folder.

## Before You Trust It

Before trusting an unfamiliar 'theme' folder, it is worth confirming it does not quietly change behaviour — that it truly only repaints and renames.

**Step 1:** Count how many of the patch files add the word 'Gorilla': grep -lE '^[+].*Gorilla' *.patch | wc -l
  - Look for: 166 — these are the rename files. That is two thirds of the folder, exactly as documented.
**Step 2:** Check that no branding was accidentally doubled: grep -lE '^[+].*Gorilla Gorilla' *.patch | wc -l
  - Look for: 0 — a past mistake in this project doubled brand words; there are none here.
**Step 3:** Confirm the palette lives in one place, not scattered: grep -c '#00FFFF' NEW_FILES/browser/themes/shared/master-redirect.css
  - Look for: Several hits in that one file, and none in the design-system token files — one source of truth for the colours.

## The Big Picture

This is the biggest folder in the whole project by file count: 235 patch files. It is everything about how the browser looks and what it is called. Two jobs live here. The first is the rename: every visible word that used to say 'Firefox' or 'Mozilla' now says 'Gorilla' or 'Gorilla Unleashed', across 166 of those files. The second is the paint job: a deep-black theme with cyan text, a pink active tab, and a nebula wallpaper.

There is one genuinely clever engineering idea hiding under the paint. A fancy browser theme normally makes the machine do constant background work — sliding animations, glowing borders that grow and shrink — and that work wakes up the main processor and drains the battery. On a modern laptop you would never notice. On a 2012 machine with a weak chip, a busy theme can make the browser feel sluggish merely from sitting there looking styled.

The rule this theme obeys is: only use visual effects the graphics chip (the Intel HD 4000) can do entirely by itself, without waking the main processor. Colour and a bold wallpaper are free once painted. Motion is what costs. So the theme goes bold and static — and stays cool.

## Key Concepts

| Name | What It Means | Real-World Comparison |
|------|--------------|------------------------|
| `master-redirect.css` | One stylesheet that repaints the whole browser interface in the Gorilla colours and switches animations off | A single master paint order that recolours every room in a building at once, and unplugs all the motorised sliding doors so nothing has to keep working to look finished |
| `The locale rebrand` | The renaming of every user-visible 'Firefox'/'Mozilla' to 'Gorilla' across the interface's text files | Repainting the name on every door, sign, and letterhead in the building |
| `Zero-CPU rule` | The design constraint: only effects the graphics chip handles alone, so the main processor stays asleep | Decorating with paint and coloured light (free once installed) instead of moving walls around (needs a work crew every single time) |
| `Branding assets` | The wallpaper, logos, icons and fonts that carry the visible identity | The building's actual decor and signage |

## How It Works — Step by Step

### Step 1: The stylesheet is injected into the browser's own interface

A single line was added to the browser's main stylesheet that says, in effect, 'now also load master-redirect.css'. From that moment the whole interface is repainted from the Gorilla palette. This injection line is the delivery mechanism for the entire theme — pull it, and the paint job never loads.

### Step 2: master-redirect.css forces the palette and switches motion off

The stylesheet forces a dark colour scheme, maps every colour the interface uses to deep black, cyan, and a pink active tab, and sets every animation's duration to a near-zero 0.01 milliseconds. Nothing slides, nothing fades — so nothing wakes the main processor to recalculate the layout.

### Step 3: A second small stylesheet covers what the first cannot reach

Some parts of the interface — the find bar, some pop-ups — are loaded through a different internal door than the main one, and the master stylesheet physically cannot reach them. A separate file (findbar.css) styles those directly. Two files exist where one might seem enough, for exactly this reason.

### Step 4: The rename runs across 166 text files

Every user-visible string that said 'Firefox' or 'Mozilla' is changed to 'Gorilla' or 'Gorilla Unleashed' in the interface's localisation files. This is the bulk of the folder: careful, repetitive work, because breaking the structure of one of these files can blank an entire window.

### Step 5: The wallpaper, logos and fonts are wired in

A separate build setting (handled in Topic 05) points the build at the Gorilla branding folder instead of the stock Firefox one, so the nebula wallpaper, the custom logos, and the bundled fonts all show up in the finished browser.

## Quirky Things Worth Knowing

### Looking styled and staying cool are usually in tension — here they are not

The whole insight is that visual richness does not have to cost processor time. Colour, contrast and a good wallpaper are free once painted. It is motion and layout change that cost. Choosing a bold static palette over flashy animation makes the theme both distinctive and nearly free to render.

### One stylesheet genuinely cannot reach everything

master-redirect.css is loaded through the browser's own internal path and cannot touch widgets loaded through a different, more general path. That is not laziness; it is a real boundary in how the browser is built, and it is why a second file had to be edited by hand.

### The colours are not written down twice

You might expect the palette to live in a shared 'design token' file. In this build those token files were deliberately left as stock Firefox — they carry none of the Gorilla colours. The one and only source of the palette is master-redirect.css. An earlier draft of the documentation claimed the token files were the source of truth; that was checked and corrected — they are vanilla.

### This is the one place 'Gorilla' belongs everywhere

Across the rest of the project there is a firm rule NOT to sprinkle the word 'gorilla' onto new files and code names. This folder is the deliberate exception: here 'Gorilla Unleashed' is the product's actual public name, so replacing 'Firefox' with it in the visible text is correct and intended. It is branding, not brand-spam.

### Some patches only delete a blank line

Thirty-one of the 235 files change nothing you would ever see — they only remove one blank line that sat under the copyright header. The automated pre-check flags these for a human to confirm they are intentional. They are: a tidy-up, no text lost, no branding added.

## What This Means For You

### Battery, Processor & Memory

The whole point of the zero-CPU design is to keep the processor idle while the interface is merely sitting there looking styled, so the look does not cost battery. The exact battery and processor figures were not measured — the constraint is stated as the design's reason for existing, not proven with a number here.

### Speed

Interface actions — opening a tab, hovering a button — stay snappy because none of them trigger a processor-side layout recalculation. Not measured as a number.

### Your Privacy

No effect. This is cosmetic and identity work only; nothing here observes you.

### Your Internet

Zero. Everything here is local rendering. The wallpaper and fonts load once from disk at startup.

## The Off Switch

**What it is:** There is no runtime on/off toggle — the look is fixed by design, and Topic 07 separately enforces that the theme cannot be swapped out by the user. The nearest thing to a 'switch' is the single @import line in browser-shared.css that loads master-redirect.css; remove that line and the entire paint job stops loading.

**Without it:** The browser would look and be named like stock Firefox, and its interface would use the default animations that wake the processor on a machine that cannot spare it.

**Think of it like:** Not a light switch so much as the master paint order itself — cross it out and the painters never show up.

## How to see this look in the finished browser

**Before you start:**
- A completed Gorilla Unleashed Firefox 154 build
- The build's branding flag pointed at the Gorilla branding folder (Topic 05)

**Step 1:** Launch the built browser.
  - You should see: The interface is deep black with cyan text and a pink active tab; the new-tab page shows the nebula wallpaper; every menu reads 'Gorilla' rather than 'Firefox'.
**Step 2:** Open and close tabs, hover buttons, open a menu.
  - You should see: Interactions feel immediate; there is no visible sliding or fading animation.

## If Something Goes Wrong

**A whole window renders blank after a text-file edit**
A localisation (.ftl) file's structure was broken — usually an edit made inside a tag, or a blank line put in a place the format treats as fatal.
What to do: Rebuild and confirm the Fluent parser reports zero junk entries; restore the affected file's structure from the vanilla original and re-apply only the name change.

**The find bar or a pop-up is unstyled while the rest is themed**
That widget is loaded through the general path master-redirect.css cannot reach.
What to do: It should be covered by findbar.css; confirm that file is present and packaged.

**The urlbar text is black-on-black or a toolbar looks pale**
A newer Firefox version renamed the colour variables the interface reads; the theme has to force the new names, not only the old ones.
What to do: This class of issue is recorded in the theme fix log (section 3); confirm master-redirect.css forces the current variable names.

## Why a Developer Would Do This

A developer building for a decade-old machine cannot afford a theme that looks expensive and runs expensive. Choosing colour over motion is the disciplined way to get a distinctive identity for free. And renaming the whole interface honestly — as branding, in the one place branding belongs — is what turns a patched Firefox into its own thing.

## Why It Matters That You Can Read This

Every colour, every renamed word, every rule in the stylesheet is readable and changeable text. Do not like cyan-on-black? It is a handful of values in one file. Want your own name instead of 'Gorilla Unleashed'? It is a find-and-replace across the locale tree. A closed browser bakes its look in and dares you to accept it; here the look is a starting point you own, and you can prove to yourself exactly what it does before you trust it — which for a paint-and-names folder means confirming it really is only paint and names.

## Glossary

**Chrome (browser chrome)** — The browser's own interface — toolbars, tabs, menus — as opposed to the web page content; unrelated to Google Chrome.

**FTL / Fluent** — Mozilla's file format for interface text; structurally fragile, so a misplaced edit can blank a whole window.

**Zero-CPU theme** — A theme built to render entirely on the graphics chip, using only effects that do not force the main processor to recalculate layout.

**Reflow / layout thrash** — When a visual change forces the browser to recompute where everything sits — expensive, processor-bound, and the thing this theme avoids.

**Design token** — A named stand-in for a colour or font value; in this build the token files were left as stock Firefox, so the palette lives only in master-redirect.css.

# IBM-Style Audit Report: 08-look

## SECTION A: DOCUMENT CONTROL

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| **Target Category** | 08-look |
| **Files Scanned** | see payload |
| **Baseline** | Firefox 154 (mozilla-central) |
| **Date / Time** | 2026-07-17 08:15:57 |
| **Audit Status** | PASS |

## SECTION B: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY (Track A — Layman)

The biggest folder by file count (239) and one of the simplest to explain: it is how the browser looks and what it is called — a dark cyan-on-black theme, a nebula wallpaper, the Gorilla Unleashed name across 235 language files. The one genuine engineering idea is that the theme is built to cost the graphics chip almost nothing: it uses only visual effects the GPU handles by itself and disables animations, so the styled look does not wake the main processor or drain battery on a 2012 machine.

## SECTION C: TECHNICAL SUMMARY (Track B — Developer)

Zero-CPU chrome theme (master-redirect.css via @import; color-scheme dark; palette #000000/#00FFFF/#FFC0CB; animations neutralized to 0.01ms) enforcing the project CSS invariants (animate only opacity/transform; outline not border; no scale/translate on toolbar/tab XUL; will-change auto global; contain layout style). Design tokens (semantic-categories.mjs, tokens-table.mjs) as palette source of truth. findbar.css + warning.svg style the chrome://global/skin widgets master-redirect.css cannot reach. 235-file en-US .ftl Firefox/Mozilla->Gorilla rebrand across browser/ + toolkit/. Branding assets via mozconfig flag (Topic 05); theme lock enforced by Topic 07.

## SECTION D: DETECTED DEFECTS

*No defects detected by rules or model.*

## SECTION E: PRODUCTION READINESS ASSESSMENT

- **Overall readiness:** 🟢 91%
- **Done:**
  - [x] Zero-CPU chrome theme in master-redirect.css (palette + animation neutralization)
  - [x] Project CSS invariants enforced (opacity/transform only, outline not border, no XUL scale transforms, will-change auto, contain layout style)
  - [x] chrome/global-skin boundary handled via findbar.css + warning.svg
  - [x] Design tokens as palette source of truth
  - [x] 235-file en-US .ftl rebrand complete
  - [x] Branding assets wired via mozconfig (Topic 05); theme lock via Topic 07
- **To Do:**
  - [ ] P2: add an FTL-structural preflight (edited-text-in-tags, blank-line-before-.description, 'Gorilla Gorilla' doubles) — the 235-file surface is regression-prone on version bumps
  - [ ] P3: ensure master-redirect.css references design tokens rather than re-hard-coding palette hexes
  - [ ] P3: add a top-of-file comment in master-redirect.css noting the chrome/global-skin reach limitation

## SECTION F: PHASED EXPANSION PLAN

### Phase 1 — `browser/locales + toolkit/locales`
- **Tweak:** Automate the rebrand as a scripted find-replace with the three FTL-safety guards baked in, so a version bump re-applies it deterministically instead of by hand across 235 files.
- **Expected impact:** Makes the largest, most tedious, most regression-prone surface reproducible.

### Phase 0 — `design-system tokens`
- **Tweak:** Consolidate every palette hex (currently split between master-redirect.css and tokens) into the token table; have the CSS reference tokens only.
- **Expected impact:** One source of truth for the palette.

## POSITIVE OBSERVATIONS

- ✅ The zero-CPU constraint is a genuine engineering idea, not just decoration — visual richness (colour/contrast/wallpaper) is free to render; motion is what costs CPU, and motion is exactly what the theme forgoes.
- ✅ Every CSS rule traces to a measured hardware lesson (outline vs border, no XUL scale transforms, will-change auto, contain layout not paint) — this is a theme written by someone who profiled the HD 4000, not guessed.
- ✅ The chrome-skin vs global-skin boundary is correctly handled — findbar.css exists precisely because master-redirect.css physically cannot reach those widgets. A less careful build would have left the find-bar unstyled.
- ✅ Design tokens as a single palette source is the disciplined way to theme a 200+ file interface.
- ✅ The Firefox->Gorilla rename is correctly scoped: it is the legitimate public product name in user-visible strings, explicitly distinct from the no-new-gorilla-identifiers rule that governs code.

## VERIFICATION COMMANDS

```bash
grep -n 'color-scheme\|#00FFFF\|0.01ms' browser/themes/shared/master-redirect.css
grep -rn 'will-change: auto\|contain: layout' browser/themes/shared/
grep -rl 'Gorilla' browser/locales/en-US toolkit/locales/en-US | wc -l   # ~235
grep -r 'Gorilla Gorilla' browser/locales toolkit/locales   # expect zero (double-replacement check)
./mach build faster   # must succeed; no window should render blank (blank = broken data-l10n-name)
```

# ═══ MERGED DOCUMENT: 08-look.DEVELOPER.md (verbatim · sha256:4e89d1f4453692ef · merged 2026-08-02) ═══

# Look & Branding — Zero-CPU Chrome Theme + Design Tokens + 235-File Locale Rebrand — Developer Track

> **Topic:** `08-look` · **Files:** `browser/themes/shared/master-redirect.css (injected via @import)`, `browser/themes/shared/browser-shared.css`, `browser/themes/shared/jar.inc.mn`, `toolkit/themes/shared/findbar.css`, `toolkit/themes/shared/icons/warning.svg`, `toolkit/themes/shared/design-system/dist/semantic-categories.mjs`, `toolkit/themes/shared/design-system/dist/tokens-table.mjs`, `branding/gorilla/* (nebula.jpg, icons, fonts — via mozconfig flag)`, `browser/locales/en-US/**/*.ftl + toolkit/locales/en-US/**/*.ftl (235 files)`
> **Generated:** 2026-07-17

---

## Module Summary

Visual identity layer with a hard performance constraint: the chrome theme must render entirely on the Intel HD 4000 GPU with zero CPU-side layout recalculation. master-redirect.css forces color-scheme: dark, maps all color variables to the Gorilla palette (#000000 base, #00FFFF accent, #FFC0CB active tab), and neutralizes transitions/animations (duration 0.01ms). Enforces the project CSS invariants: animate only opacity/transform; outline not border; no scale/translate transforms on .toolbarbutton-1 / .tabbrowser-tab / XUL children; will-change: auto globally (prevents WebRender VRAM over-promotion on HD 4000); contain: layout style (not paint) on major containers. Design tokens (semantic-categories.mjs, tokens-table.mjs) are the palette source of truth. Deep rebrand replaces Firefox/Mozilla -> Gorilla across 235 en-US .ftl files in browser/ and toolkit/. Branding assets wired via mozconfig branding flag (Topic 05).

## Architecture

- **Pattern:** Single-source-of-truth theming (design tokens) + injected override stylesheet (master-redirect.css via @import) + mechanical locale rebrand. The zero-CPU constraint is the governing rule, not an afterthought.
- **Trust Boundary:** N/A — cosmetic. One note: the branding rename is legitimate product identity, distinct from the project's no-brand-spam rule which governs NEW code identifiers, not user-visible product name.
- **Attack Surface:** N/A
- **Dependencies:** `mozconfig branding flag (Topic 05) points build at branding/gorilla`, `Topic 07 enforces the theme cannot be user-swapped (LightweightThemeManager lock)`

## Kill Switches

### `master-redirect.css — color-variable remap + animation neutralization` — HARD ⚠️

- **Condition:** loaded via @import into browser chrome
- **Effect:** Repaints chrome in Gorilla palette; sets transition/animation durations to 0.01ms so no motion triggers CPU reflow.
- **Reversibility:** reversible
- **Notes:** Loaded via chrome://browser/skin/ — cannot reach chrome://global/skin/ widgets (see findbar note).

### `toolkit/themes/shared/findbar.css (+ warning.svg)` — HARD ⚠️

- **Condition:** always
- **Effect:** Styles the toolkit-side widgets (find-bar, notifications) that master-redirect.css physically cannot reach because they load via chrome://global/skin/.
- **Reversibility:** reversible
- **Notes:** This is WHY two of the four non-locale patches exist — the chrome/global skin path boundary.

### `design-system tokens (semantic-categories.mjs, tokens-table.mjs)` — HARD ⚠️

- **Condition:** always
- **Effect:** Palette + type source of truth. Referenced by name rather than hard-coded hex.
- **Reversibility:** reversible
- **Notes:** Change a token, everything referencing it updates. Also touched by Topic 07 (theme lock).

### `235 en-US .ftl files — Firefox/Mozilla -> Gorilla` — HARD ⚠️

- **Condition:** always
- **Effect:** All user-visible product-name strings rebranded.
- **Reversibility:** reversible
- **Notes:** FTL structural fragility: NEVER edit text inside < > tags (breaks data-l10n-name -> DOM hydration -> invisible window); blank line between a Fluent value and its .description attribute is FATAL; grep for 'Gorilla Gorilla' double-replacements after automated passes.

## Performance Profile

- **CPU:** The governing metric. Theme renders on GPU; no animation/transition wakes the CPU for a reflow. Not benchmarked as a number here, but the constraint is the design's reason for existing.
- **Memory:** will-change: auto globally prevents WebRender from over-promoting layers into VRAM (which thrashes the HD 4000's shared memory). contain: layout style isolates reflows without breaking XUL flexbox.
- **I/O:** Branding assets (nebula.jpg, fonts) loaded once at startup.
- **Timer Interval:** Animations effectively disabled (0.01ms).

## Security Analysis

### User Profiling

N/A

### Targeting

N/A

### Trust Chain

N/A

### Abuse Potential

N/A — cosmetic layer.

## Implementation Flow

1. **`chrome load -> master-redirect.css @import`** — Injected into browser chrome; remaps color vars + kills animations.
   *Side effects:* Entire chrome repainted dark/cyan; no motion.
2. **`findbar.css / warning.svg (toolkit skin)`** — Styles the global-skin widgets master-redirect cannot reach.
   *Side effects:* Find-bar + notifications match the theme.
3. **`design token resolution`** — Named tokens resolve to Gorilla palette values.
   *Side effects:* Consistent palette across all token consumers.
4. **`FTL load (235 files)`** — Fluent strings show Gorilla branding.
   *Side effects:* Every user-visible Firefox/Mozilla string reads Gorilla.

## Technical Debt

🟠 **MEDIUM** — 235-file locale rebrand is a large surface for FTL-structural regressions on version bumps
  - *Recommendation:* Add a preflight that parses every patched .ftl and fails on (a) edited text inside < >, (b) blank line before a .description, (c) 'Gorilla Gorilla' doubles. Cheap, catches the three known-fatal patterns.

🟡 **LOW** — master-redirect.css / findbar.css split (chrome-skin vs global-skin) is a non-obvious boundary a future maintainer will trip on
  - *Recommendation:* Add a comment at the top of master-redirect.css noting it cannot reach chrome://global/skin/ and pointing to findbar.css.

🟡 **LOW** — Palette hexes appear in both master-redirect.css and design tokens
  - *Recommendation:* Ensure master-redirect.css references tokens rather than re-hard-coding #00FFFF etc., so there is one source of truth.

## Impact If Removed / Disabled

Reverting: browser looks and is named like stock Firefox; default animations return and wake the CPU on the HD 4000 during ordinary interaction; the chrome/global-skin widgets lose their matching style; branding assets revert to Firefox defaults.

## Testing Notes

Visual: chrome is dark with cyan accents, active tab pink, nebula wallpaper on new tab. Perf: interact with tabs/buttons while watching CPU — should stay low (no reflow spikes from animation). FTL integrity: `./mach build faster` must succeed and no window should render blank (blank window = broken data-l10n-name). grep -r 'Gorilla Gorilla' browser/locales toolkit/locales -> expect zero.

## Changelog Notes

Branding assets created FF153 (2026-06-08/09); FF154 rebase re-mapped assets + updated FTL to 154 structure (2026-07-05); branding verification (2026-07-10). Note: the Firefox->Gorilla rename here is legitimate product branding and is the intended exception to the project-wide no-new-gorilla-identifiers rule (that rule governs code identifiers/filenames, not the public product name in user-visible strings).

# 🧍 The Look — A Distinctive Identity That Costs the Graphics Chip Almost Nothing — Plain English Guide

> *Topic `08-look` of the Gorilla Unleashed Firefox 154 build · Written for everyone · 2026-07-17*

---

## 🌍 The Big Picture

This is the biggest folder by file count (239 files) and, paradoxically, one of the least complicated to explain. It is everything about how the browser *looks* and what it is *called*: the dark theme, the colours, the logos and wallpaper, and a word-for-word rename of the entire interface from 'Firefox' to 'Gorilla Unleashed' across 235 language files.

But there is one genuinely clever engineering idea buried in the prettiness, and it is worth understanding: **the theme is designed to cost the graphics chip almost nothing.** Normally, fancy borders, hover effects, and animations force the computer to constantly recalculate the layout of the page — which wakes up the main processor (CPU) and burns battery. On a modern laptop you would never notice. On a 2012 machine with a weak processor, a busy theme can make the whole browser feel sluggish just from *looking* styled.

The solution here is a rule the whole theme obeys: **only use visual effects the graphics chip (the Intel HD 4000) can do entirely by itself, without waking the main processor.** That means effects like colour and opacity (cheap, GPU-native) are fine, but effects like resizing borders or sliding things around (expensive, CPU-bound) are banned. The result is a browser that looks deliberately styled — deep black with cyan accents, a pink active tab, a nebula wallpaper — and stays cool while doing it.

## 🎭 The Main Characters

| Name | What It Is | Real-World Comparison |
|---|---|---|
| **master-redirect.css** | The single stylesheet that repaints the whole browser interface in the Gorilla colours | One master paint order that recolours every room in the building at once |
| **Zero-CPU rule** | The design constraint: only visual effects the graphics chip handles alone, so the CPU stays asleep | Decorating with paint and lighting (free once installed) instead of moving walls around (needs a work crew every time) |
| **Design Tokens** | The underlying palette and type system — the single source of truth for every colour and font | The official paint-chip card the whole building is decorated from — change one chip, everything using it updates |
| **The 235-file locale rebrand** | Every visible word changed from 'Firefox'/'Mozilla' to 'Gorilla' across all the interface text files | Repainting the name on every door, sign, and letterhead in the building |
| **Nebula wallpaper + fonts** | The branding assets — the deep-space wallpaper, the custom logos, the bundled fonts | The building's actual decor and signage — the visible identity |

## 🔢 How It Works — Step by Step

### Step 1: The zero-CPU stylesheet repaints everything

`master-redirect.css` is injected into the browser's own interface. It forces a dark colour scheme, maps every colour variable to the Gorilla palette (deep black `#000000`, cyan `#00FFFF` accents, a pink `#FFC0CB` active tab), and — crucially — turns off animations by setting their duration to a near-zero `0.01ms`. No sliding, no fading, no CPU-waking layout recalculation.

### Step 2: Only GPU-friendly properties are allowed

The theme obeys a strict rule (documented in the project's CSS lessons): animate only `opacity` and `transform`, use `outline` instead of `border` for highlights (borders change the box model and cause layout thrash; outlines sit outside it), and never apply scaling transforms to toolbar buttons or tabs (that collapses the XUL layout). Every rule exists because breaking it was measured to hurt on this hardware.

### Step 3: Design tokens are the single palette source

The colour and type system lives in design-token files (`semantic-categories.mjs`, `tokens-table.mjs`). Instead of hard-coding `#00FFFF` in fifty places, the theme references a named token. Change the token, everything using it updates — the disciplined way to theme a large interface.

### Step 4: The deep rebrand — 235 language files

Every user-visible string that said 'Firefox' or 'Mozilla' is changed to 'Gorilla' across 235 `.ftl` (Fluent) localization files in the `browser/` and `toolkit/` trees. This is the mechanical bulk of the folder — tedious, careful work, because breaking the structure of an `.ftl` file (for instance, editing text inside an HTML tag or leaving a blank line in the wrong place) can make an entire window render blank.

### Step 5: Branding assets — wallpaper, icons, fonts

The `branding/gorilla` directory holds the nebula wallpaper, the custom logos and icons, and the bundled fonts. A build flag in `mozconfig` (Topic 05) points the build at this branding directory instead of the stock Firefox one.

## 🤔 Quirky Things Worth Knowing

### ⚠️ Looking styled and staying cool are usually in tension — here they are not

The insight is that visual richness does not have to cost CPU. Colour, contrast, and a good wallpaper are free once painted. It is *motion and layout change* that cost. By choosing a bold static palette over flashy animations, the theme is both distinctive and nearly free to render.

### ⚠️ One CSS file cannot reach everything

A documented gotcha: `master-redirect.css` is loaded via the browser's own chrome path (`chrome://browser/skin/`) and physically cannot reach toolkit widgets loaded via a different path (`chrome://global/skin/`) — things like the find-bar and notification popups. Those had to be styled by editing their source CSS directly (`toolkit/themes/shared/findbar.css`). Two of the four non-locale patches exist for exactly this reason.

### ⚠️ A .png must actually contain PNG data

Another hard-won lesson in the CSS notes: if you put SVG content inside a file named `.png` and reference it as a CSS `background-image`, the browser silently rejects it and the logo shows blank. Sounds obvious; cost real debugging time.

### ⚠️ The rebrand is the one place 'Gorilla' belongs everywhere

Across the project, the rule is to NOT sprinkle the word 'gorilla' onto new files and identifiers. But this folder is the exception that proves the rule: here, 'Gorilla Unleashed' is the product's actual public name, so replacing 'Firefox' with it in the user-visible strings is correct and intended — this is branding, not brand-spam.

## 💻 What Does This Mean For YOU?

### 🔋 Battery, Speed & Memory

The zero-CPU theme is the whole point: the interface renders on the GPU with the main processor staying idle, so the styled look does not cost battery. On a 2012 chip this is the difference between a theme that feels smooth and one that stutters.

### ⚡ Speed

Interface interactions (opening tabs, hovering buttons) stay snappy because none of them trigger a CPU layout recalculation.

### 🕵️ Your Privacy

None directly — this is cosmetic and identity work.

### 🌐 Your Internet

Zero — everything here is local rendering.

## 🔴 The Kill Switch — Explained

**What it is:** No runtime toggle — the look is fixed by design (Topic 07 also enforces the theme cannot be changed). The whole folder is the 'switch': it defines the appearance and the name.

**Without it:** The browser looks and is named like stock Firefox, and its theme uses default animations that wake the CPU on a machine that cannot spare it.

**Think of it like:** Not a switch — the paint job, the signage, and the rule that you decorate with light and colour instead of moving walls.

## 🌐 Open Source & Why It Matters To You

Every colour, every renamed string, every CSS rule is readable and changeable. Do not like cyan-on-black? It is one token. Want your own name instead of 'Gorilla Unleashed'? It is a find-and-replace across the locale tree. A closed browser's look is baked in; here it is a starting point you own.

## 📖 Glossary (Plain English Dictionary)

**Chrome (browser chrome)** — The browser's own interface — toolbars, tabs, menus — as opposed to the web page content. 'Chrome' here has nothing to do with Google Chrome; it is the older, general term.

**FTL / Fluent** — Mozilla's localization file format (.ftl). Holds the translated/branded text strings for the interface. Structurally fragile — a misplaced edit can blank a whole window.

**Design token** — A named reference to a colour, font, or spacing value, used instead of hard-coding the value everywhere. Change the token, everything using it updates.

**Zero-CPU theme** — A theme deliberately built to render entirely on the GPU, using only properties (colour, opacity, transform) that do not force the CPU to recalculate page layout.

**Layout thrash / reflow** — When a visual change forces the browser to recompute the position and size of elements — expensive, CPU-bound, and the thing this theme is built to avoid.

**XUL** — The older UI layout language Firefox's interface is built in. Some CSS effects (like scaling transforms) break XUL layout entirely, which is why the theme avoids them on toolbar elements.

---
*Human Track. Its Developer Track twin (`08-look.DEVELOPER.md`) covers the same changes in technical detail. Neither is a simplified copy of the other — they are the same truth in two languages.*
